react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on a single dominant biological signal: arachidonic acid metabolism via the eicosanoid synthesis axis. In run_ramp_enrichment, WikiPathways 'Eicosanoid synthesis' (WP:WP167) achieved the top rank with an FDR of 1.25×10⁻¹³ and a fold-enrichment of 1429, driven by five co-abundant lipid mediators from the input list — arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), 5(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04805), 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2 (KEGG:C14717). The same five compounds appeared as the `metabolites_hit` roster in SMPDB NSAID-action pathway analogues (aspirin, rofecoxib, acetaminophen) and in the Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency pathway, all sharing the same FDR floor (3.28×10⁻¹³). Mummichog independently scored 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' as the top network hit (p=0.00328) with 100% overlap — all 11 matched compounds in that pathway were drawn from the input set. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned 'hsa00590' as the top entry (p=0.0684), with arachidonate, LTA4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE as the matched members. Histamine (KEGG:hsa00340, rank 2 in MetaboAnalystR) independently scores the histidine metabolism branch consistent with inflammatory immune activation alongside the eicosanoid cluster. Dihydrothymine (KEGG:C00906) maps to pyrimidine catabolism (KEGG:hsa00240) but lacks statistical support from ORA tools. Gentisic acid (KEGG:C00628) appears in phenylalanine/tyrosine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00350, p=0.171) as a peripheral phenolic outlier. Copper (KEGG:C00070) and hypochlorite (KEGG:C19697) were not captured by any pathway-enrichment tool — both are trace-element or reactive-species entities poorly represented in current metabolic network libraries. The cross-paradigm consensus is unambiguous: the treatment group is characterised by coordinated activation of the COX/LOX eicosanoid axis with arachidonic acid at the substrate hub.
